items.q: What fake metric traps knowledge workers?
items.a: **Pseudo-productivity** — visible busyness, meetings, and email responsiveness inherited from agriculture/industry — while real value comes from **deep work**: sustained, distraction-free cognitive effort. Newport estimates **~4–4.5 hours/day** of peak cognitive output (Huberman ~**3–4 h**).

items.q: Why are smartphones so expensive for focus?
items.a: They induce costly **attention-network switching** and create **solitude deprivation** — no time free from other minds' stimuli — locking you into all-day social-processing mode that drives anxiety and exhaustion. The tax is switching cost, not just minutes on screen.

Fix your **concentration budget** in advance and **pull** tasks from an active list (e.g. Trello) instead of drowning in push-based email/meeting bombardment. Newport calls email a **public post to-do list**.

items.q: How does multiscale planning beat a naked to-do list?
items.a: Cascade **seasonal/quarterly objectives → weekly plan against the real calendar → daily time blocks**. Assign work to actual free hours: short gaps → admin; first **~90 min** → hardest deep work.

items.q: What does a shutdown ritual actually include?
items.a: End-of-day **loop closure**: review inbox/plan/calendar, capture open loops, preview tomorrow, then a demonstrative **"work is over"** signal. Associating the dinner table with work thoughts poisons relationships and sleep (Matt Walker parallel).

items.q: Is flow the state that makes you better?
items.a: No — Newport says **deliberate practice** (maximal discomfort, Anders Ericsson) is the opposite of flow's time-dissolving ease. Pros push ~**20% past comfort**; growth requires discomfort, not just enjoyable immersion.

items.q: Can individual willpower fix a hyperactive hive-mind workplace?
items.a: Often not. Constant email/Slack/Zoom is like neglecting a **$20M factory robot**; escaping needs expensive **top-down workflow redesign**. *Slow Productivity* prescription: fewer commitments, longer timelines, obsession with **quality over visible activity**.

items.q: What environment tweaks protect deep work?
items.a: Prefer **silence** (lyrical music hurts focus), engineer windows/blinds to cut visual distraction, and for digital minimalism run a **30-day** reset by aggressively pursuing **replacement activities** — white-knuckle abstinence alone fails. The better you get, the more the world steals the time that built your reputation.
